We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions to synthesize target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We have already identified a disconnection: The first step (retro) could be cleavage of the C-N bond between aromatic amine and amide carbonyl (amide bond). Using template 647549 (amide bond cleavage) gave precursors: O[C:7]([c:6]1[n:2]([CH3:1])[n:3][n:4][cH:5]1)=[O:8] (which is a carboxylic acid? Actually O- attached to carbonyl) and [NH2:9][c:10]1... which is an aniline? The result from apply_template gave: ('COc1cccc(N)c1', 'Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O') Wait earlier apply_template gave ('COc1cccc(N)c1', 'Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O') Actually after applying template 647549 to the amide-containing substructure (COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1) we got two fragments: 'COc1cccc(N)c1' (an aniline with methoxy) and 'Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O' (a triazine? Actually it's a 1,2,4-triazol-3-yl carboxylic acid). Good.

Now we need further disconnections to get to simple purchasable precursors, total 3 reactions (so 2 retrosynthetic steps after this? Actually route must have 3 reactions total, meaning we need three steps forward synthesis. So retrosynthesis will have three layers: target -> step1 precursors (two fragments) -> step2 each fragment further broken -> step3 final building blocks.

We have fragments:

Fragment A: COc1cccc(N)c1 (4-methoxyaniline). This is commercially available (is_buyable true). So we can consider it as a starting material, no further disconnection needed.

Fragment B: Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O (a 1,2,4-triazol-3-yl carboxylic acid with an amino substituent). Need to connect to the side chain Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 (aryl-CH2- attached to triazole). Actually original target has c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N: the triazole is substituted at N with a benzyl group bearing a side chain (CN4...). So our fragment B is missing that benzyl substituent. The amide carbonyl attached to triazole N? Wait original: NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the amide carbonyl attached to the triazole carbon (C=O attached to N? Actually NC(=O) attached to triazole carbon (c2). The triazole has N at position 1? Anyway.

Our retro step gave Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O which is triazole-3-carboxylic acid with an NH at position? It lacks the benzyl substituent. So we need to introduce the benzyl group via a substitution (Sn2) on the benzyl halide onto the triazole nitrogen? Actually the original has N-alkylation of triazole nitrogen with benzyl group (C attached to aromatic ring). So we can propose a retrosynthetic step: N-alkylation of triazole (nucleophilic N) with benzyl chloride (or bromide) to give N-benzyl triazole. That matches Sn2 reaction described. So we need to find a template for N-alkylation of heteroaryl nitrogen with alkyl halide. Search for template where functional group broken is alkyl halide, formed is N-alkyl bond. Use search with functional_groups_broken ["alkyl halide"] and functional_groups_formed maybe ["aryl amine"?]. Let's search.
